facility_roles.quote: The higher energy and intensity evolution of AdA, ADONE, started the study of the electron-positron collisions physics in Frascati.

intervals.label: ADONE data taking (first generation)
intervals.note: The INFN-LNF page dates the first and second generation experiments together ('from 1969 to 1978'); no source gives this experiment's own end date, so 1978 is the latest possible end and the interval is approximate.
intervals.quote: The experimental activity on ADONE with colliding beams began in 1969 with four experiments

intervals.label: data taking ended

intervals.quote: The first generation experiments, and successively the second generation ones, explored the physics of electron-positron collisions up to 3.0 GeV in the center of mass, from 1969 to 1978.

physics_goals.quote: The "Gamma-Gamma" Experiment (with researchers from Frascati and Rome) had, as a principal goal, the detailed study of reactions with neutral particles in the final state.
physics_goals.value: Reactions with neutral particles in the final state of e+e- annihilation

summary.plain: One of the four first experiments at Frascati's ADONE collider (1969), by researchers from Frascati and Rome, built to study e+e- reactions with neutral particles such as photons in the final state.
summary.technical: Gamma-Gamma at ADONE (first generation, 1969): scintillator counters behind lead converters and spark chambers for reactions with neutral final states; Frascati and Rome group. Its natural development was Gamma-Gamma 2.
